corrections.text: The Overview quotes Cloudflare's blog post as stating "since the platform launched in 2017, a Worker could open outbound sockets to a database or a service, but it could only be a server for HTTP." That sentence does not appear in Cloudflare's post; it is InfoQ's wording. Cloudflare's own post instead says: "Ever since Workers launched in 2017, we've been expanding their capabilities, including adding the ability to open outbound TCP connections and a JavaScript-native RPC system built on Cap'n Proto." The underlying fact — that this is the first time Workers can act as a server for a non-HTTP protocol — is accurate and independently reported by InfoQ; only the attribution to Cloudflare directly was wrong.

The "gRPC arrives as the first protocol on top" section quotes "web platform APIs like fetch() do not expose" and "which is why gRPC-web exists" as Cloudflare's own words. Both phrasings are from InfoQ's analysis, not Cloudflare's post. Cloudflare's post reads "Web platform APIs like fetch() don't provide this control," and attributes the "why X exists" reasoning to the WebSocket API, not to gRPC-web specifically.
